subject.title: fix(github-copilot): reject unvalidated OAuth enterprise domain on refresh

question: Should current main retain any executable legacy GitHub Copilot OAuth profile path, or should doctor/migration invalidate those profiles and require conversion to the plugin-owned token profile before any token use?
rationale: Current main has changed the provider ownership and credential shape since this branch’s base, so a maintainer must choose whether the legacy runtime remains supported or is migration-only debt; that choice determines where the complete fail-closed boundary belongs.

options.title: Invalidate and reauthenticate
options.body: Recommended: migrate or mark legacy OAuth profiles unusable in doctor and require plugin-owned token reauthentication before refresh or model traffic.

options.title: Retain guarded legacy runtime
options.body: Rebase the legacy OAuth implementation and reject unsupported persisted origins consistently before refresh, model routing, and every bearer-bearing request.

options.title: Close as obsolete
options.body: Close this PR only after source and upgrade proof shows current main cannot load or execute any legacy OAuth profile and already gives affected users a recovery path.

recommendation.title: Invalidate and reauthenticate
recommendation.body: Recommended: migrate or mark legacy OAuth profiles unusable in doctor and require plugin-owned token reauthentication before refresh or model traffic.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision crosses the current provider-plugin owner boundary, legacy credential compatibility, and security policy rather than being a test-only repair.
